annotations.title: Is an employer on an official visa sponsor register?

description: For up to 100 employer names, whether each appears on an official government sponsor register JOA reads: the UK Home Office register of licensed sponsors, the IND recognised sponsors (NL), the SIRI fast-track certified companies (DK) (licences), and the US DOL LCA (H-1B) and PERM filings, the Canadian positive LMIA employers and the Irish employment permits (filing evidence, not a licence). Works for any employer, with or without JOA jobs. Each result is matched (JOA found the register entry that is this employer by its name), ambiguous (a register entry has this name, contains it, or differs from it only by a legal form or a word such as Group, Holdings, International or UK, and JOA cannot confirm it is this employer: same-name entries are in hits with ambiguous true, the others in possible_names, hits can be empty; never a silent pick), not_found (no entry of the registers read has this name and none contains it), excluded (franchise brand, staffing firm or recruiter, too short a name) or no_register (JOA reads no register for that country: unknown, not a no). A name sent with its legal form matches only the entry that prints that name: Group, Holdings, International, UK and country words count and plc is not Ltd (Rolls-Royce Holdings plc is not Rolls-Royce plc); such a twin is listed in possible_names with a hint and never matched, with or without a town. A name sent without a legal form matches when exactly one entry answers and it has two or more words or 10 or more characters; a single shorter word is ambiguous until the town is added. Each hit is one printed register name and says matched_on (legal_name, trading_name or alias: an English name of a Dutch institution mapped to its IND register name) and match_type: exact_legal_name (the name sent is the printed legal name word for word; safe to accept) or exact_normalised (equal once legal forms and words such as Group or UK are set aside: a match on a brand name; show legal_name or check it). There is no fuzzy matching. A name of another country or with a foreign legal form is not_found (AstraZeneca UK Limited is not AstraZeneca B.V.). possible_names and suggested_name are leads, never matches: suggested_name is set when exactly one register name is, or contains, the name sent without a legal form (Monzo gives Monzo Bank Ltd); check it is the employer, then call again with it as the name. Never report an ambiguous result or a suggested_name as a match. hint says what to send next (often: add the town). One bad employer never fails the call: it is answered with status invalid (reason and hint say what is wrong) and the others are looked up; status error means that one employer could not be looked up this time. Neither is charged. region is only used for the US. A hit means the employer appears on the official register as of the date given; it never means the employer will sponsor a particular role, so never say it will. Every answer carries legal_note_code (immigration_information) and legal_note: this is information only, not immigration or legal advice and not a service to candidates, and it may be wrong or out of date; when you pass results to a jobseeker, include the legal_note text. Costs 0.1 record per employer, rounded up per call, on every plan including the free one. NEEDS a JOA API key.

employers.description: 1 to 100 employers. Each: name (required, legal or trading name), country (ISO two-letter: GB, US, NL, IE, CA, DK; omit to read every register), town, region (US state).

country.description: ISO 3166 two-letter country of the register (GB, US, NL, IE, CA, DK).

name.description: Employer name as you hold it.

region.description: US state, two letters or in full.
